title: Win architecture and commercial ask template for inference deals
author: Marissa Chen
content:
Purpose
-------
This document is a reusable seller artifact for technical and commercial conversations where a customer is evaluating an inference platform. It combines a concise win architecture (how we integrate), a structured pilot ask, commercial/price guidance, and short security FAQ and objection-handling. Use this as the canonical 'ask & slides' template when preparing an enterprise pilot or sales engineering discovery.

Executive one-liner
-------------------
Redwood Inference provides predictable, production-grade LLM inference that reduces per-token costs and stabilizes latency at scale by combining dedicated runtime optimizations, workload-aware batching, and automated routing across hosted/dedicated/private modes.

Audience-specific elevator pitches
----------------------------------
- CTO / Platform: 'We give you a single API and deployment model that preserves SLAs while reducing unit inference costs by 20–60% vs unmanaged endpoints, and lets you pin model versions for reproducible rollouts.'
- ML/AI Engineer: 'Ship features faster: same API for hosted and private deployments, automatic KV/prefix caching, and model lifecycle tools (versioning + canary) so you don't rebuild infra between experiments and prod.'
- Engineering Manager: 'Cut inference spend and reduce unpredictable regressions with per-route observability and automated fallback policies for availability.'
- CFO / Procurement: 'Pilots start usage-based with optional reserved capacity for predictable monthly commitments. Typical pilot TCO case reduces token spend and hardware overhead vs self-host by 25–50% in first 6 months.'

Key differentiators to emphasize
-------------------------------
- Unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments (same API/observability).
- Cost controls: intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, model quantization recommendations.
- Reliability: routing policies + automatic fallbacks to compatible variants and regions.
- Developer experience: SDKs, prompt set evals, and per-token tracing to debug cost and latency hot paths.

Competitive brief (short)
------------------------
Competitor landscape and short messaging to use in conversations:
- Major cloud AIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google): Strength = model quality and ecosystem; Risk = cost unpredictability, limited private deployment options; Redwood = lower cost controls + private deployment options + observability.
- Cloud managed endpoints (SageMaker endpoints, Vertex AI): Strength = deep cloud integration; Risk = fragmentation and heavy ops for model variants; Redwood = opinionated runtime that reduces operator burden and improves unit economics.
- Self-hosted inference stacks / runtimes: Strength = control; Risk = engineering time and maintenance; Redwood = delivers similar control with a managed control plane and ops tooling to reduce maintenance.

Pilot (POC) ask template — technical + commercial
--------------------------------------------------
1) Technical scope (what we need from the customer):
   - 1–3 representative workloads (prompts/payloads) and associated SLOs (target p95 latency, request concurrency).
   - Dataset or prompt deck for quality regression checks (200–1k prompts).
   - Access: sample API keys / sandbox credentials and an integration point (API route, batch export, or internal message bus).
   - Security baseline: IP allowlist, required KMS integration (Y/N), SOC2 requirements.
2) Pilot duration and success metrics (recommendation):
   - Duration: 4–8 weeks.
   - Success metrics: latency p95 <= target; quality delta within agreed tolerance (BLEU/ROUGE or human-eval); cost per effective token reduced by X% vs baseline; error rate and availability targets.
3) Commercial ask (pilot economics templates):
   - Option A — Consumption pilot: Hosted usage billing (per-token, per-embedding) with free support hours and 30-day trial credits.
   - Option B — Reserved pilot: Small dedicated pool (e.g., 4–8 A100-equivalent GPUs) for 8 weeks at discounted commitment (typically 20–40% below list for dedicated).
   - Commercial ask sample language: 'We propose a 6-week reserved pilot at $XXk/month or a consumption pilot with $Yk in credits and no upfront commit. If success metrics are met, we request a commercial decision window and a 12-month reserved capacity commit.'

Pricing guidance and TCO scenarios (quick examples)
--------------------------------------------------
- Micro pilot (Proof-of-value): 4 weeks, consumption model, estimated spend $3k–15k depending on throughput.
- Standard reserved pilot: 8 weeks, 4 GPU-equivalent, discounted rate $25k–60k total (negotiated).
- Scale annual reserved: Commit to 24/7 capacity with unit rates 30–60% lower than consumption in typical benchmarks.
- TCO note: Include engineering ops cost avoided (estimate 0.5–2 FTE depending on customer maturity) in the conversation — quantify in dollar terms when possible.

Sample slide deck outline (10 slides)
------------------------------------
1) Title & ask (one slide): pilot length, commercial ask, and success metrics.
2) Customer problem + data (latency/cost pain).
3) Redwood solution overview (runtime + routing + observability).
4) Win architecture (diagram: request flow, caching layer, model variants, fallback path).
5) Pilot scope & timeline (detailed week-by-week).
6) Pricing scenarios & ask.
7) Risk & mitigation (security, privacy, performance).
8) Success metrics & evaluation plan (how we measure quality).
9) Customer references / quick case summary.
10) Next steps & decision points.

Win architecture (example – standard integration)
------------------------------------------------
- Front door: Customer app -> Redwood API (or VPC peered Private control plane).
- Routing: Policy-based routing to hosted/dedicated/private pool.
- Runtime: Dedicated GPU pool with batch scheduler, KV cache, quantized model variants for low-latency fallbacks.
- Observability: Per-request token breakdown, p95/p99 latency, per-route cost.
- Ownership: SE owner (sales), ACE (solutions engineer), CSM assigned post-pilot.

Case study vignette (one-slide summary style)
--------------------------------------------
Customer: Nimble Retail (hypothetical)
Problem: Product search recommendations were 200–400ms tail latency with high per-query cost.
Pilot approach: 6-week reserved pilot, cohort of 50k monthly queries, progressive canary (10% -> 100%).
Outcomes: p95 latency reduced from 420ms to 180ms, per-query inference cost dropped 42%, integrated fallback for overloaded models reduced error spikes during peak events.
Metric callouts: 42% cost reduction, 57% p95 latency improvement, 99.95% availability during pilot.

Security FAQ (concise answers for prospect review)
------------------------------------------------
Q: Can you run in our VPC / on-prem?
A: Yes. Redwood supports Private deployments (VPC and on-prem packaging) with customer-managed networking and optional air-gapped builds.
Q: How do you handle keys?
A: Integrates with customer KMS/HSM for model encryption and runtime key handling. Keys never leave the customer KMS unless explicitly authorized.
Q: Auditability and logs?
A: Full audit logging available via the private control plane; hosted customers can export detailed access logs and per-token usage events.
Q: Data residency and retention?
A: Configurable retention windows and region pinning. For sensitive workloads, we recommend Private deployment and explicit data retention policies.
Q: Regulatory evidence?
A: We provide standard compliance artifacts (SOC2 Type II report, penetration test summaries) and a redacted evidence pack under NDA where required.

Objection handling cheatsheet
----------------------------
- "We can self-host cheaper" -> Ask about ops/maintenance burden, and present 12-month TCO with FTE savings. Share a 6–12 month break-even analysis.
- "We need on-prem only" -> Highlight Private deployment options and typical delivery timeline (8–12 weeks for on-prem packaging + validation).
- "Model quality worries" -> Offer A/B evals and rollout canaries; propose an initial split-run experiment.

Sales readiness checklist (pre-call)
----------------------------------
- Artifacts to have: customer prompt deck, baseline cost/latency numbers, target SLOs, security checklist.
- People to align: SE, solutions architect, legal (if customer requires NDA or data processing agreement).
- Slides: bring the 10-slide deck with explicit commercial ask slide.

Ownership & next steps
----------------------
- Template owner: Marissa Chen (go-to-market).
- When to use: Any enterprise prospect where integration or pilot is required, especially platform/vertical accounts.
- Ops: After pilot kickoff, route handoff to CSM and create a short 90-day runbook for migration to reserved capacity.

Appendix: sample commercial ask language (copy/paste)
---------------------------------------------------
'We propose a 6-week reserved pilot at $45k total (covers dedicated pool and support). If the pilot meets the success metrics above, Redwood requests a decision to convert to a 12-month reserved commitment at the negotiated unit rates within 30 days of pilot completion.'

End of document
